account.activity.title: Recent activity
account.password.changed: Password changed.{count, plural, =0 {} one { # other device was signed out.} other { # other devices were signed out.}}
account.password.title: Change password
account.profile.emailFixed: Changing your email address isn't available yet.
account.profile.title: Profile
account.sessions.intro: Every device signed in to your account. If you do not recognise one, sign it out and change your password.
account.sessions.title: Active sessions
account.title: Account
app.notFound.title: Not found
auth.forgot.sent: If that address has an account, a reset link is on its way.
auth.forgot.title: Reset your password
auth.forgot.tooManyRequests: Too many requests. Try again later.
auth.reset.badLink: The link is incomplete or has expired.
auth.reset.title: Choose a new password
auth.tooManyAttempts: Too many attempts. Try again later.
auth.tooManyAttemptsFor: Too many attempts. Try again in {seconds, plural, one {# second} other {# seconds}}.
auth.verify.goHomeForNewLink: Go home and request a new link
auth.verify.incomplete: The link is incomplete. Request a new one.
auth.verify.verified: Your email address has been verified.
boms.batchAmountsNote: Enter batch amounts, not amounts per unit. Starts as a draft: add components, then promote it.
boms.empty: No recipe yet. A recipe is what makes a production run one click instead of typing the components every time.
boms.external.tooltip: Provided by whoever manufactures — never enters our stock
boms.licence.help: What this formulation is registered under.
boms.licence.helpNew: What this formulation is registered under. Leave blank if it is not.
boms.licence.stillChangeable: Still changeable: nothing has been made against this version yet.
boms.line.againstBatch: Against the batch size, not one unit.
boms.line.externalNote: An external component never enters our stock and no movement is written for it, but it stays on the recipe so the batch record is complete.
boms.line.inUnit: In {unit} — what this item is counted in.
boms.makesPerBatch.help: How many this recipe produces in one run — 1000, not 1.
boms.newVersion.tooltip: An active recipe cannot be edited — this copies it to a new draft
boms.noComponents: A recipe with no components cannot be promoted — it would make stock appear from nothing.
boms.promote.tooltip: Makes this the recipe new runs use, and archives the current one
common.decimal.grouped: Type the number without separators between thousands, as in {example}.
common.name: Name
components.colorMode.label: Colour mode
components.currency.label: Currency
components.documentLanguages.second.help: For a bilingual sheet: each label in both.
components.errorBoundary.title: Something went wrong
components.errorBoundary.updated: The app was updated while this tab was open. Reload to pick up the new version — nothing is lost.
components.formError.label: Error
costs.allCosted: Everything on hand has a cost.
costs.intro: Each lot carries what it cost; stock without lots carries a running average. Values are material cost only — what was bought and what went into a batch — in the base currency.
costs.lot.waiting: Part of this lot is still waiting for a cost. Set it on the <link>Stock value</link> page.
costs.noBaseCurrency: No base currency yet, so nothing can be valued. Set one on the <link>Organization</link> page.
costs.run.provisional: Something this run used was still waiting for a cost when it was consumed, so these figures are low. Setting that cost now records the difference, but does not change this batch.
costs.run.whatWeSupplied: What we supplied. Components the manufacturer provided, and any charge for making it, are not included.
costs.set.price.help: Per unit, as the supplier charged it.
costs.set.rate.help: {base} per {currency}. Leave blank to use the rate on file for the day it arrived.
costs.set.title: Set cost
costs.why.adjustment: Counted in, with nothing to value it by
costs.why.noRate: Priced in {currency}, with no rate on file
costs.why.production: Made by a run that is still open
inventory.actions.label: Actions for {sku} at {location}
inventory.history.introLot: Every movement of lot {lot}, newest first. Nothing here can be edited or removed — a correction is another movement that says so.
inventory.history.introVariant: Every movement of {sku}, newest first. Nothing here can be edited or removed — a correction is another movement that says so.
inventory.history.title: History for {sku}
inventory.leavesOnly: Only locations that hold stock directly are listed.
inventory.lot.changesEverywhere: This changes the lot everywhere, not only the units at {location}.
inventory.lot.codeEditable: Nobody printed this code, so a typo can be corrected here.
inventory.lot.codePrinted: Printed on the boxes, so it cannot be renamed. Move the stock to the correct lot instead.
inventory.lot.expires.help: Leave blank if it does not expire.
inventory.lot.expires.helpReceive: Leave blank if it does not expire. Ignored if this lot already exists.
inventory.lot.number.help: As printed on the box. Receiving the same lot again adds to it.
inventory.lot.title: Lot {code}
inventory.move.adjust.title: Correct the count
inventory.move.difference.help: How many {unit} out, not the new total.
inventory.move.givenTo.help: Optional. Recorded so a recall can find it.
inventory.move.heldBack: {location} is marked not available, so nothing can be sent from it. Move the stock to an available location first.
inventory.move.sample.title: Send a sample
inventory.move.ship.title: Ship out
inventory.move.transfer.title: Move to another location
inventory.move.whatHappened.help: Whoever reads this in six months was not there.
inventory.movements.empty: Nothing has moved yet. Receiving stock is what puts the first row here.
inventory.movements.intro: Every quantity change, newest first. Movements are never edited or removed — a mistake is corrected by another movement.
inventory.needsLocation: Add a location before receiving stock. Stock sits in the places that contain nothing else — a bin, a shelf, or a whole warehouse if you have not divided it up yet.
inventory.promised.intro: Across every location stock can be sent from. Held stock is for a confirmed sale, earliest confirmed first; free stock can be promised, sampled or used in production.
inventory.promised.title: Promised to customers
inventory.receive.noProducts: No products yet. Add one on the Products screen — stock is counted against a variant, so there has to be something to count.
inventory.search.help: Anywhere in the SKU, the product name or the lot code.
inventory.trace.cameFrom.empty: No receipt or production is recorded for this lot. It may have been counted into stock by a correction.
inventory.trace.lotCode.help: Any part of the code works — the batch number is usually enough. Press Enter to search.
inventory.trace.madeFrom.empty: Not made in a run here — received, not produced.
inventory.trace.receivedBy.empty: Nothing from this lot has left the business.
inventory.trace.receivedBy.intro: This lot and everything made from it: the list a recall has to reach.
inventory.trace.receivedNoOrder: Received with no order on record
inventory.trace.title: Trace a lot
inventory.trace.unknownRecipients: Some left with no recipient on record — shipped without an order, or sampled without a name. They are listed below with no partner.
inventory.trace.whereNow.empty: None of this lot is on hand anywhere.
invoices.credit.priceRule: The price can be lowered — a restocking fee, goodwill, a price correction at the difference — but never raised.
invoices.credit.title: Credit {number}
invoices.draft.deleteNotice: Nobody outside has seen it, and it has no number yet. The shipment can be invoiced again afterwards.
invoices.empty: No invoices yet. Open an order and create one from a shipment.
invoices.filter.label: Invoice status
invoices.intro: An invoice bills one shipment, and is created from it on the order. Once issued it never changes — a mistake is voided with a credit note and invoiced again.
invoices.issue.intro: {partner} will be invoiced {amount}. Once issued it gets its number and cannot be edited; a mistake is corrected by voiding it with a credit note.
invoices.issue.title: Issue this invoice?
invoices.issue.untaxed: {skus} {count, plural, one {has} other {have}} no tax code yet.
invoices.note.help: Printed for the customer: a PO number, a thank-you.
invoices.previewNote: What issuing will store, calculated the same way.
invoices.taxCode.applied: Tax code set on every line
invoices.taxCode.none: No tax codes yet — add them in Tax codes.
invoices.void.intro: A credit note for {amount} reverses it in full. Both stay on record. The shipment can then be invoiced again, or voided itself.
invoices.void.reason.help: Printed on the credit note, so the customer reads it.
invoices.void.title: Void {number}?
invoices.voidedNoDate: Voided: {reason}. The credit note below reverses it in full.
invoices.voidedOn: Voided {date}: {reason}. The credit note below reverses it in full.
language.label: Language
layout.notifications.title: Notifications
layout.unverified.message: Confirm your email address to secure your account.
locations.code.help: What is on the label — H5, A-01-03. Unique within its parent.
locations.create.leavesHoldStock: Stock sits in the places that contain nothing else. A single room is a location in its own right — add bins inside it later if you need them.
locations.create.parentStopsHolding: {name} will stop holding stock directly. Anything already there has to move into a child location first.
locations.create.title: Add a location
locations.edit.inside.help: Its own descendants are not listed — moving a location inside itself would detach the subtree.
locations.edit.title: Edit {name}
locations.empty: No locations yet. Start with a site — a building or an address. You can add zones, aisles, and bins inside it later, or leave it as one room.
locations.type.help: A label for reading, not a rule. Depth is not enforced.
orders.close.purchase: Some of what was ordered has not been received. Closing the order says nothing more is expected — the stock already received stays exactly as it is, and anything that turns up later can be received from the Inventory screen.
orders.close.sale: Some of what was ordered has not been shipped. Closing the order says nothing more will be sent — what has shipped stays exactly as it is, and anything sent later can be shipped from the Inventory screen.
orders.close.title: Close this order?
orders.closeLine.notice: The ordered quantity stays as it is. Nothing further will be expected, but the shortfall remains visible — otherwise a short delivery would look the same as an accurate one.
orders.closeLine.title: Stop expecting the rest
orders.closeLine.why.help: Discontinued, backordered indefinitely, ordered by mistake.
orders.create.isSample: This is a sample — price it at zero if it is free
orders.create.loadFailed: Could not load partners and products.
orders.direction.purchase.help: Stock arrives, and is received against this order.
orders.direction.sale.help: Stock leaves. Receiving does not apply to a sale.
orders.duplicate.advice: Fix the draft, confirm it, then cancel this one — that way nothing is lost if something goes wrong.
orders.duplicate.intro: A new draft for {partner}, with the same {count, plural, one {item} other {# items}} and quantities. This order is not changed.
orders.duplicate.notCopied: The reference and expected date are not copied. A supplier's PO number belongs to the order it was issued against.
orders.duplicate.reference.optional: Optional — you can add it later.
orders.duplicate.reference.used: The original used {reference}. The copy needs its own.
orders.duplicate.title: Duplicate this order
orders.edit.fixed: The supplier and direction cannot change — every line and every receipt is recorded against them. Duplicate the order instead.
orders.edit.reference.help: The supplier's PO number, or your own. Shown in the orders list.
orders.edit.title: Edit order
orders.empty.open: Nothing open. Raising an order records what you asked a partner for — receiving against it is what puts the stock on a shelf.
orders.filter.label: Show
orders.lines.catalogueFailed: Could not load the catalogue. Close and try again.
orders.lines.confirmedNotice: This order has been confirmed. Changing the quantity or price amends what was agreed with the supplier.
orders.lines.draftPurchase: Nothing can be received against a draft. Confirming is what says this order is real.
orders.lines.draftSale: Nothing can be shipped against a draft. Confirming is what says this order is real.
orders.lines.heldTooltip: {held} held for this order; the rest waits for stock
orders.lines.noPrices: No prices recorded on this order
orders.lines.partialTotal: Some lines have no price — this is not the full total
orders.lines.price.help: Optional. Left blank, the order's price list supplies it when there is one.
orders.lines.price.keep: Leave blank to keep the current price.
orders.lines.returnsNote: Returns don't reopen an item. To send replacements, raise a new sale.
orders.receive.note.help: Damage, a short count, anything the ledger should say.
orders.receive.title: Receive {sku}
orders.return.againstRma.help: If the customer was authorized to send this back. It is then held to what the RMA allows.
orders.return.notOnRma: Not on {rma} — leave it empty, or receive it without the RMA
orders.return.notRestocked: Nothing is restocked here. Once checked, move it to a shelf, or correct the count if it is being written off.
orders.return.note.help: What the customer said, or what you found in the box.
orders.return.nothingShipped: Nothing has shipped on this order, so nothing can come back.
orders.return.putIn.help: Usually a bin marked not available, so nothing ships it again before it is checked.
orders.return.rmaAllows: {rma} authorizes {quantity}, {received} back against it so far
orders.returns.linkIntro: Received {date}: {items}. A return is counted against one RMA, once.
orders.returns.linkTitle: Link this return to an RMA
orders.returns.onceOnly: A return is counted against one RMA, once.
orders.ship.mustAddUp: Must add up to {quantity}. The server checks when you ship.
orders.ship.noLots: No lots of this at the chosen location.
orders.ship.together: Everything listed ships together, or nothing does. Set a line to 0 to leave it for a later shipment.
orders.ship.tooMany: More than the {quantity} still outstanding. The server will refuse it.
orders.shipments.empty: Nothing has shipped against this order yet.
orders.shipments.title: Shipments
orders.shipments.voidedNote: Voided {date}: {reason}. Everything on it went back where it came from.
orders.theirReference.help: Their number for this order, not ours. Optional.
orders.void.reopens: This order is closed. Voiding reopens it, since what it was closed on never left.
orders.void.title: Void this shipment
orders.void.warning: Only for a box that has not left. Everything on it goes back where it came from and the order can ship again. The shipment stays on the order, struck through, with your reason. If the box did leave and came back, take a return instead.
orders.void.why.help: Customer cancelled before pickup, recorded on the wrong order, clicked too early.
partners.address.label: Label
partners.address.label.help: What you would call it out loud — Head office, Dock 3.
partners.addresses.empty: No addresses yet. An order needs somewhere to ship to.
partners.code.help: Your own reference — a supplier number, a customer code. Unique within your organization if you use one.
partners.contact.phone.help: An email or a phone — at least one.
partners.contact.role.help: In their words — Accounts payable, Warehouse manager.
partners.contacts.empty: No contacts yet. Someone has to answer when an order is late.
partners.create.oneList: One list for both sides of the trade. There is nothing to pick here — whether this partner is a supplier or a customer follows from the orders you raise against them.
partners.create.title: Add a partner
partners.documentLanguages.notice: Packing slips, invoices and credit notes for this partner, from the next one made. Those already made keep their languages.
partners.documentLanguages.title: Document languages
partners.edit.title: Edit {name}
partners.empty: No partners yet. Add the firms you buy from and sell to — an order needs one before it can be raised. The same partner can be both.
partners.name.help: Names are not unique — two branches of one company are two partners.
partners.taxId.help: VAT, GST, EIN — whatever applies. Stored as typed, never validated.
production.cancel.issuedStay: The components already issued stay where the run is. Cancelling does not carry them back — somebody has to move them.
production.cancel.title: Cancel this run
production.cancel.why.help: The first thing whoever finds the leftover material will ask.
production.close.intro: Enter what was actually used. Anything left as planned is recorded as planned.
production.close.overPlan: Using more than planned is fine — the extra is taken from the same place the rest came from. Anything left over stays where the run is and needs putting away by hand.
production.close.title: Close this run
production.create.location.help: Components are issued here and output is received here.
production.create.manufacturerNote: Only set a manufacturer when we supply some of the components. If they buy everything and deliver finished goods, that is a purchase order.
production.create.noRecipe: No promoted recipe for this item. You can still plan the run, but releasing it needs a recipe — there would be nothing to issue.
production.create.quantity.help: How many finished units this run should produce.
production.create.quantity.scales: The recipe makes {quantity} per batch — components scale to whatever you enter.
production.create.recipe.help: An archived version is offered for repeating an old batch.
production.create.reference.help: A batch number or the maker's works order. Optional.
production.draftNotice: Nothing has moved yet. Releasing copies the recipe onto this run and issues the components.
production.empty: Nothing here. A run consumes components and produces a finished item — it needs a recipe first, which lives on the product.
production.external.tooltip: Never enters our stock, so nothing is consumed for it
production.finished: Finished. {produced} produced against a plan of {planned}.
production.licence.allow: {problem} Your organization allows releasing under it; the run will record that it was {state, select, expired {expired} other {not yet in force}}.
production.licence.block: {problem} Your organization does not release runs under it.
production.licence.blockWithdrawn: {problem} Nothing can be made under it.
production.licence.canOverride: {problem} You can release under it with a reason, which is kept on the run and shown wherever the batch is traced.
production.licence.missing: This recipe carries no licence, and your organization requires one before a run is released. Attach one to the recipe first.
production.licence.needsOverride: {problem} Releasing under it needs an override from someone allowed to give one, with a reason.
production.licence.reason.help: For example: renewal filed 3 Sept, confirmed by the regulator.
production.noLinesYet: Components appear once the run is released — they are copied from the recipe then, so editing it afterwards cannot change this run.
production.output.sameBatch: Same batch unless this part was genuinely separate.
production.output.soFar: {produced} recorded so far against a plan of {planned}.
production.output.staysOpen: The run stays open until you close it, so a batch made over several days is recorded a bit at a time.
production.output.title: Record output
production.release.amountsInvalid: Enter each amount as a number, up to four decimal places.
production.release.chosenMismatch: Chosen {chosen} of {needed} — the amounts must add up exactly
production.release.copiesRecipe: Releasing copies the recipe onto this run and moves the components to where it is made. Editing the recipe afterwards will not change what this run consumed.
production.release.earliestFirst: Lot-tracked components are taken earliest expiry first.
production.release.noRecipe: There is no recipe for this item yet. Create one on the product's page and make it active, then release.
production.release.nothingConsumed: Nothing is consumed yet — that happens when you close the run, with the amounts actually used.
production.release.recipe.help: This run was planned without one. It is attached before releasing.
production.release.short: This location is {amount} short across all its lots.
production.release.title: Release this run
production.release.tooltip: Copies the recipe onto this run and moves components to it
production.variance.components: {count, plural, one {One component was} other {# components were}} well off plan: {list}. Recorded as it happened — worth a look at the recipe or the batch.
production.variance.output: This run made {produced} against a plan of {planned} — {percent} off. Worth checking the yield on the recipe, or whether output was recorded twice.
products.create.title: Add a product
products.discontinuedNotice: This product is discontinued. Its variants keep their own status, so reactivating restores each to what it was.
products.sku.help: Typed, not generated — this is the code on the label.
products.tracksLots.fixed: Lot tracking cannot be changed later.
products.translations.descriptionNeedsNa: A description in {language} needs a name in {language} too.
products.translations.intro: Where a language is left blank, documents in it print the base name, {name}.
products.translations.none: None yet: every document prints the name above.
products.translations.title: Names in other languages
products.variant.unitsPerCase.help: How many of this variant ship in one case.
products.variation.helpOptional: Optional. 60ct, Large, Blue — leave blank if there is only one.
rmas.cancel.notice: Says it never happened: nothing came back and nothing was credited. It stays on record, marked cancelled.
rmas.cancel.title: Cancel {rma}?
rmas.close.notice: Says nothing more will happen under it — no more goods back, no more credit. What was received and credited stays as it is.
rmas.close.title: Close {rma}?
rmas.filter.label: Return authorization status
rmas.goodsComeBack: Goods come back through Take a return on the order, naming {rma}.
rmas.intro: Return authorizations: what a customer may send back, and whether it is credited, replaced or neither. Raise one from the sale it concerns.
rmas.keepOrDestroy: The customer was told to keep or destroy the goods, so nothing will be received. Credit follows what is authorized.
rmas.link.intro: For goods that arrived before this RMA was raised. A return is counted against one RMA, once.
rmas.link.noneLeft: Every return on this order already counts against an RMA.
rmas.link.title: Link a return to {rma}
rmas.raise.expectsGoods: The customer is sending the goods back
rmas.raise.invoice.help: Optional. The credit defaults to it.
rmas.raise.keepOrDestroy: Told to keep or destroy them: credit then follows what is authorized here, since no box will arrive to be received.
rmas.raise.title: Authorize a return
rmas.raise.why.help: What the customer said: cracked in transit, wrong item, expired on arrival.
